text:
Marathon Petroleum dropped 0.7% today to $427.34, marking the third down day in a volatile two-week stretch that's seen the stock lose 10%. The stock moved on the heels of quarterly earnings announced today and a leadership change, along with a quarterly financial report filing. The broader refining backdrop remains mixed: US crude is trading at $103.37 per barrel while refineries are running at a healthy 92.8% capacity, but global crude at $123.10 signals persistent international weakness that can constrain export-dependent refiner margins.

The timing matters here—the earnings announcement and management shift came as energy stocks more broadly faced caution from analysts, who have warned that guidance and forward outlook could disappoint even as Big Oil's third-quarter numbers look strong on paper. The recent volatility in the stock price (jumping from $432 to $444 just days ago, then sliding back down) suggests investors are still digesting what the new leadership and guidance mean for future returns.
